intro: Medical assistants combine patient care, office work and coordination, a strong base for nursing and technical health careers. The closest of the 25 careers below is Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses, with a 92% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $64,400, which is 41% more than the $45,690 medical assistants earn.
why_it_works: A clinic day means rooming patients, taking vital signs, explaining instructions and keeping the schedule on track. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4 out of 5 for this job, and service orientation and coordination at 3.5. Nursing, imaging and respiratory therapy use those same patient skills. Most matches need no new degree, though licenses require training. The gaps are quality checks and equipment work.
tips: Ask your employer about tuition help for LPN programs; many clinics support assistants who train further.
MRI technologists earn $95,480, which is 109% more, and are a 71% match.
Medical Records Specialists earn $51,140, or 12% more, if you prefer office work.

faq.q: What jobs can former medical assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are licensed practical nurses (92%), ophthalmic medical technicians (86%) and Registered Nurses (84%), based on O*NET 31.0. Medical Records Specialists are also 84% matched and earn $51,140, which is 12% more than the $45,690 medical assistant median.

faq.q: Which careers for medical assistants pay more?
faq.a: 14 of the 25 matches pay more. Registered Nurses earn $97,550 (114% more), MRI technologists $95,480 (109% more) and Respiratory Therapists $82,280 (80% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Registered nursing usually needs a bachelor's degree, while MRI and respiratory programs are shorter.

faq.q: Do medical assistants need more education to switch?
faq.a: For most paths, no degree is needed. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than medical assistants already have, though nursing and imaging need a license. In the closest match, 38% of workers have some college courses, and many LPN programs take about a year.

faq.q: What skills should medical assistants learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, equipment maintenance, equipment selection and judgment and decision making. Coordination already rates 3.5 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so clinical and technical training is the main step toward better-paid roles.
